summary: This is the pandas 2.2.1 API reference page for pandas.Series.all, which returns whether all elements are True, optionally over an axis. It describes the axis, bool_only, skipna and kwargs parameters, the return value, and examples for both Series and DataFrame. The surrounding navigation and footer text is site boilerplate.
one_line: pandas 2.2.1 API reference page for Series.all, which tests whether all elements of a Series or DataFrame axis are True.
key_facts: The page is the pandas 2.2.1 API reference entry for pandas.Series.all.
Series.all returns True unless at least one element within a series or along a DataFrame axis is False or equivalent (e.g. zero or empty).
The axis parameter defaults to 0, and for Series this parameter is unused.
Setting axis=None reduces all axes and returns a scalar.
The bool_only parameter defaults to False and is not implemented for Series.
The skipna parameter defaults to True and excludes NA/null values.
If the entire row or column is NA and skipna is True, the result of Series.all is True, as for an empty row or column.
If skipna is False, NA values are treated as True, because they are not equal to zero.
Additional **kwargs have no effect but might be accepted for compatibility with NumPy.
For a DataFrame with col1 [True, True] and col2 [True, False], df.all() returns col1 True and col2 False.
df.all(axis=None) returns False for that DataFrame.
